summary: Iteration 25 — Verified the four additive enhancements (checkout destination, verification workflow, Tenant Admin role, per-account audit view). Backend: existing 8 tests in test_payment_acceptance.py + 17 tests in test_capture_void.py PASS (25/25). Added 3 new additive tests in test_iter25_additive.py covering public checkout acceptance payload (populated + null), and Tenant Admin role permissions — ALL 3 PASS. Frontend: on /dashboard/payment-acceptance, created a fresh unverified UPI account, confirmed Verify button (acceptance-verify-{id}) is visible, clicking it emits success toast 'Verification requested — status is now pending', badge switches to 'pending', Verify button disappears (never auto-'verified'). History icon (acceptance-history-{id}) opens acceptance-audit-dialog listing two rows (create + request_verification) with timestamps + actor email; VPA is masked in changes ('ui****@yesbank') — full VPA never present.
critical_code_review_comments: checkout.py public_get_session builds acceptance dict inside a single ternary line — readable but consider factoring into a helper if more fields are added (non-blocking).
PaymentAcceptance.jsx audit dialog uses raw JSON.stringify of the changes blob; a compact key/value renderer would be friendlier, but masking is correct and no full VPA leaks (non-blocking).
seed_data_creation: 3 additive backend tests create ephemeral acme acceptance accounts (VPAs like chk*@yesbank). Frontend test created one UPI account 'UI Verify Test' under the currently active tenant and moved it to verification_status=pending. No production data touched.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Payment Acceptance additive feature (verify + audit view + checkout destination + Tenant Admin role) is fully validated. Testids for the two new interactions: acceptance-verify-{id}, acceptance-history-{id}, acceptance-audit-dialog, acceptance-audit-row-{id}, acceptance-audit-empty. Public checkout GET returns additive 'acceptance' object (or null). Tenant Admin role includes payment_acceptance_account.view/.manage. Note: /api/roles returns permissions as list of {code,description,module,id} dicts, not plain strings — use p['code'] when asserting.
